title: Ang 8: Japji ends, So Dar begins
hook: the last salok, then the first evening hymns
tomorrow: who's speaking when the evening hymns change voice?

segments.voice: A week of pages, gathered up. A clean place to keep them. Aloud and silent. Read together, stumbles and all. Begin at the beginning, where it begins: without fear, without hate. And yesterday, japji on the page, where no one stands outside the hukam. Now, the Japji's last page.
screen: `A CLEAN PLACE · ALOUD AND SILENT · READ TOGETHER.` → `BEGIN AT THE BEGINNING · WHERE IT BEGINS.` → `JAPJI, ON THE PAGE.`

segments.voice: Some phones slip into a darker screen at sunset on their own, no button pressed. The day hands over to the evening and you barely notice the seam. Ang eight has a seam like that, on paper. Near the top, the morning prayer is finishing. Lower down, a new heading appears, and the evening has started.
screen: `THE SCREEN DIMS AT SUNSET.` → `A SEAM ON ONE PAGE.` → `MORNING FINISHES. EVENING STARTS.`

segments.voice: The Japji closes with a salok. In the original: pavan guroo paanee pitaa maataa dharat mahat. Air is the Guru, water the father, earth the great mother. Then, in paraphrase, day and night are the two nurses, and the whole world plays in their lap. A few lines later the Japji is done. And on the same page comes a new heading, raga Asa, and the first of the evening hymns: So Dar. It opens with a question, in paraphrase: what is that door, what is that house, where you sit and care for all? Something to tell someone tonight: the Japji's last salok names day and night as the world's two nurses, and on that very page the evening hymns begin. The morning and the evening prayers aren't in two books. They touch on one page. Morning meets evening.
screen: `AIR, WATER, EARTH: THE LAST SALOK.` · `DAY AND NIGHT, THE TWO NURSES.` · `A NEW HEADING: SO DAR.` · then, large: `MORNING MEETS EVENING.`

segments.voice: Listen to one sound: your own breath, the air the salok calls the Guru. Don't change it; just hear it come in and go out, like day handing over to night. If you have the page in front of you, rest your eyes on the place where the Japji ends and So Dar begins.
Ang 8. The page where the Japji's last salok ends and So Dar, the first evening hymn, begins. Today's word.
Your line: morning meets evening. Day and night, the two nurses, on one page. Until next week.
